caption:
Month one will not look like winning. Here is what actually happens.

WEEKS 1–2 — nothing launches. Measurement goes in first, because without it you cannot tell a win from luck, and you will spend the next three months arguing about which one you had.

WEEKS 3–4 — first campaigns go live, and most of them lose money. That is not failure, that is the price of finding the one that doesn't. Anyone who tells you their first test wins is describing a coincidence.

MONTH 2 — you kill roughly 70% of what you launched and move the budget behind what survived. This month usually looks worse on a chart and is the most valuable one.

MONTH 3 — the first month that looks like a business. Cost per customer settles into a range, and you can finally forecast instead of hope.

Anyone promising you month-one results is selling you month three and hoping you don't count.

Slow is not the same as not working. But you only get to tell the difference if you measured in week one.
